payload.summary: All six amendments have technical merit. The highest-severity issues are that core biological limitation code still uses whole-tank totals instead of concentrations, and schema-2 saves are now hard-rejected despite an available migration path. The remaining amendments are valid reviewability, documentation, and maintainability concerns, with the repeated water-volume recomputation being low severity but still a real inefficiency.

votes.rationale: Each TankState concentration helper recomputes water_volume_l(), and that in turn re-sums substrate depth across all layers. TankSnapshot::from_state calls many of these helpers back-to-back, so the same invariant work is repeated unnecessarily. This is a small performance and code-hygiene issue rather than a correctness bug, but computing volume once and reusing it is the cleaner design.

The review diff mixes the concentration-helper refactor with major simulation-tuning changes: AOB/NOB/comammox growth yields jump from 0.001/0.001/0.0008 to 0.05/0.04/0.03, and nitrifier growth is also modified by a new carrying-capacity term. Those are materially behavior-changing adjustments. Even if the new tuning is desirable, combining it with the helper work makes regression attribution much harder.

The code still feeds Monod terms with total-mass values, and the fields are named accordingly, but half-saturation constants are conceptually concentration parameters. The current ProcessParams doc comments are therefore easy to misread as physically canonical rather than an interim approximation. A brief note that these are temporary total-mass parameterizations pending the deferred concentration-based conversion would reduce future calibration and maintenance mistakes.

The soft_acidic preset now doubles alkalinity, DIC, and bicarbonate, and its profile note shifts from roughly KH 1.5 and TDS 90 to KH 3.0 and TDS 120. That may be an intentional correction, but it is still a materially user-visible data change that affects default scenarios. The rationale should be documented or isolated so downstream chemistry changes are attributable.

The new concentration helpers are not yet the canonical basis for limitation kinetics. nitrogen_cycle.rs, algae_growth.rs, and plant_growth.rs still feed half-saturation and Monod calculations with whole-tank totals, so two tanks with the same concentrations but different water volumes still get different biological limitation factors. That preserves the underlying scientific correctness bug the helper layer was supposed to address.

SaveFile::from_json now blanket-rejects schema-2 saves, and the tests explicitly lock that behavior in. But a schema-2 save still contains the information needed for a deterministic migration: gross volume can be recovered from geometry, net volume can be computed from geometry plus substrate depth, and the existing water rescaling helper can convert totals. Turning a units refactor into a hard load failure for every existing save is an avoidable compatibility regression.
